name: Submodule target guard
summary: Reject newly introduced Git submodules with relative, mutable, local, or insecure targets.
description: A deterministic Claude Code PreToolUse gate that reconstructs .gitmodules changes and inspects static submodule-add commands, blocking new relative URLs, local paths, insecure transports, branch tracking, or dynamic targets.
risk_reason: This automatic gate rejects newly introduced Git submodules with relative, mutable, local, or insecure targets; a false denial can interrupt legitimate work, but it does not execute the blocked action.
refuses: It does not clone, fetch, initialize, update, remove, or approve a Git submodule.
It does not contact a remote or prove that a permitted remote repository is trustworthy.
It does not infer a safe target from shell variables, command substitution, aliases, or prompt text.
It does not expose a repository-owned bypass list for submodule destinations.

entrypoints.purpose: Validate bounded submodule configuration and commands before introducing mutable or unsafe repository targets.

operational.latency_reason: The entrypoint handles one intercepted event to reject newly introduced Git submodules with relative, mutable, local, or insecure targets without deferred work.
